name: Swamp / bayou
notes: Warm-temperate to subtropical forested wetland: flood-tolerant cypress-tupelo canopy on permanently or seasonally inundated soil, willow and buttonbush fringe, duckweed and floating plants, Spanish moss. Drawn on the Louisiana bayous, Okefenokee, Florida cypress domes and the Pantanal/Amazon varzea fringe.

canopy.name: Bald cypress
canopy.source: Taxodium distichum, bald cypress, dominant deciduous conifer of SE US swamps, buttressed with knees, 20-40 m — Wikipedia / USDA

canopy.name: Water tupelo
canopy.source: Nyssa aquatica, water tupelo, swollen-based co-dominant of cypress-tupelo swamps, SE USA, 20-30 m — Wikipedia / USDA

canopy.name: Black willow
canopy.source: Salix nigra, black willow, riverbank and swamp-edge tree of E North America, 10-20 m — Wikipedia / USDA

canopy.name: Pond cypress
canopy.source: Taxodium ascendens, pond cypress, dominant of Florida cypress domes and Okefenokee, 10-25 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Water elm
canopy.source: Planera aquatica, water elm/planertree, small tree of SE US swamp margins, 8-15 m — Wikipedia / USDA

canopy.name: Cabbage palm
canopy.source: Sabal palmetto, cabbage palmetto, fan palm of Florida/Gulf coast swamp hammocks, 10-20 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Buttonbush
shrub.source: Cephalanthus occidentalis, buttonbush, shrub standing in shallow swamp water across E North America, 1.5-4 m — Wikipedia / USDA

shrub.name: Virginia willow
shrub.source: Itea virginica, Virginia sweetspire, swamp understory shrub of SE USA, 1-3 m — Wikipedia / USDA

shrub.name: Wax myrtle
shrub.source: Morella cerifera, southern wax myrtle, evergreen shrub of SE US swamp margins, 2-6 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Saw palmetto
shrub.source: Serenoa repens, saw palmetto, clumping fan palm of Florida/Gulf coastal swamp hammock edges, 1-3 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Giant cane
shrub.source: Arundinaria gigantea, giant river cane, native bamboo canebrakes on SE US floodplain and swamp edges, 2-8 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Cypress knees
ground.source: Taxodium distichum pneumatophore 'knees', woody root projections around bald cypress in standing water — Wikipedia

ground.name: Duckweed
ground.source: Lemna minor, common duckweed, floating carpet on still swamp water worldwide — Wikipedia

ground.name: Lizard's tail
ground.source: Saururus cernuus, lizard's tail, emergent herb of shallow swamp water E North America, 0.3-1 m — Wikipedia / USDA

ground.name: Royal fern
ground.source: Osmunda spectabilis (regalis), American royal fern, swamp and bog fern of E North America, 0.6-1.5 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Pickerelweed
ground.source: Pontederia cordata, pickerelweed, emergent of shallow swamp margins, Americas, 0.5-1.2 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Water hyacinth
ground.source: Pontederia (Eichhornia) crassipes, water hyacinth, floating rosette native to Amazon basin, naturalised in Gulf bayous — Wikipedia

epiphyte.name: Spanish moss
epiphyte.source: Tillandsia usneoides, Spanish moss, grey festoons on cypress and oak in SE US swamps — Wikipedia / USDA

epiphyte.name: Resurrection fern
epiphyte.source: Pleopeltis polypodioides, resurrection fern, epiphytic on live oak and cypress limbs SE USA — Wikipedia

epiphyte.name: Butterfly orchid
epiphyte.source: Encyclia tampensis, Florida butterfly orchid, epiphyte on cypress and pop ash in Florida swamps — Wikipedia
